claims: An Individual Retirement Account (IRA) is a tax-advantaged personal savings account allowing individuals to invest for retirement independent of employer-sponsored plans.
Traditional IRAs offer tax-deferred growth.
Roth IRAs offer tax-free growth.
IRA contributions require having earned income.
2026 IRA contribution limit is $7,500 per year.
2026 IRA contribution limit for individuals age 50 or older is $8,600.
Traditional IRA contributions may be tax-deductible.
Tax-deductible Traditional IRA contributions reduce current taxable income.
Traditional IRA earnings grow tax-deferred.
Traditional IRA withdrawals in retirement are taxed as ordinary income.
Roth IRA contributions are made with after-tax dollars.
Roth IRA contributions have no immediate deduction.
Roth IRA earnings grow tax-free.
Qualified Roth IRA withdrawals in retirement are entirely tax-free.
IRAs are opened through financial institutions such as banks, mutual fund companies, or stockbrokers.
Earned income for IRA contributions includes wages, salaries, and self-employment income.
Anyone can open a traditional IRA.
Roth IRA contribution eligibility depends on modified adjusted gross income (MAGI).
Traditional IRA contribution deduction eligibility depends on modified adjusted gross income (MAGI).
Withdrawing earnings or contributions from a Traditional IRA before age 59½ often triggers a 10% penalty plus taxes.
IRA annual contribution limits are lower compared to 401(k) plans.
IRAs do not receive employer matching contributions unlike 401(k)s.
SEP IRA is for self-employed individuals or small business owners.
SEP IRA allows higher contribution limits.
SIMPLE IRA is a retirement plan for small businesses.
SIMPLE IRA allows both employer and employee contributions.
